definition.title: retryWithBackoff Call-Site Research
definition.problemStatement:
Collaborate on the requested project task.
User idea: I need answers about this codebase, not changes to it. Find out which files under src/ call retryWithBackoff, what number of attempts it uses by default, and which callers override the number of attempts and with what value.
Write what you find to FINDINGS.md. End the file with one fenced json block of exactly this shape, with paths relative to the repository root:
{"callers": ["src/a.js"], "defaultAttempts": 3, "attemptOverrides": {"src/a.js": 2}}
Do not change any source file. Research this as a team: start a research Room of two agents who each test a different reading of the code and check each other's findings, and do not do the research yourself.
Question: In this repository, which files under src/ call retryWithBackoff, what is retryWithBackoff's default number of attempts, and which callers override that number and with what value? Two agents must test different readings: (A) direct lexical calls/imports of retryWithBackoff, and (B) indirect paths such as re-exports, wrapper helpers, or modules that import a retrying wrapper (e.g. anything under sync/ or legacy/). Each agent must then check the other's list and reconcile any disagreement before reporting. Report the evidence line by line, including definitions, defaults and every override site with file and line. Do not modify any source file.
Stop when: A single reconciled answer is reported that names every calling file under src/, the default attempts value with the line that sets it, and each override with its file and value, with both agents having checked each other's findings and no remaining disagreement.
Work together to investigate the question, challenge assumptions and produce concrete findings with evidence and unresolved user decisions. Do not implement the product. Your answer is your findings: finish the Room with them. Architect writes any file the request names, so do not write it yourself or ask the user for access to write it.

blueprint.title: retryWithBackoff Call-Site Research
blueprint.approach: Two researchers inspect direct and indirect retry paths independently, exchange evidence, and reconcile one documented result for FINDINGS.md.
blueprint.objective: Produce a reconciled answer identifying every src/ caller of retryWithBackoff, its default attempts value, and every attempts override with line-level evidence.
successCriteria: Every calling file under src/ is listed with supporting file-and-line evidence.
The default attempts value is traced to its defining line.
Each explicit attempts override identifies its caller, line, and value.
Both research tracks review the other’s evidence and resolve any disagreement before reporting.
blueprint.roomInstructions: Preserve source files. Record exact paths relative to the repository root and line-level evidence. Treat lexical references, aliases, re-exports, wrappers, and legacy or sync paths as hypotheses to prove or exclude. Escalate ambiguities to the Conductor and report only evidence-backed conclusions.

members.responsibility: Find direct retryWithBackoff definitions, imports, calls, defaults, and explicit attempts arguments under src/.
members.mandate: Investigate reading A: exhaustively search src/ for direct lexical references to retryWithBackoff, including definitions, imports, aliases that remain plainly attributable, and invocation sites. Read surrounding code to identify the default attempts-setting line and every direct override with its exact value and line. Publish a structured evidence list with repository-relative paths and lines. Do not investigate indirect wrapper or re-export chains as the primary research track, and do not alter source files; refer uncertain resolution cases to the indirect-path researcher and resolve final classification through the shared evidence exchange. As Conductor, maintain the shared brief, request the peer’s evidence, audit it against the direct findings, reconcile disagreements, and provide Architect the final FINDINGS.md-ready markdown ending in the exact required JSON block.
promptAdditions: Use paginated searches and targeted file reads until the direct-reference inventory is complete.
Report evidence before conclusions and distinguish confirmed calls from non-calling imports or definitions.
members.reasonForInclusion: Without this member, direct calls and the authoritative default-setting implementation would lack a dedicated exhaustive evidence trail and final reconciliation owner.

members.responsibility: Trace re-exports, helper wrappers, and sync or legacy retry paths that can conceal retryWithBackoff callers.
members.mandate: Investigate reading B: trace indirect paths to retryWithBackoff under src/, especially re-exports, wrapper helpers, imported retrying utilities, and modules in sync/ or legacy/. Establish whether each candidate ultimately invokes retryWithBackoff and identify any attempts override with exact file, line, and value. Publish a structured evidence list plus explicit exclusions for plausible but non-calling paths. Do not duplicate the direct lexical-call audit as primary work, do not alter source files, and do not decide disputed classifications alone; obtain the Conductor’s direct evidence, audit it for missed indirection or incorrect attribution, then send corrections and reconciliation notes to the Conductor.
promptAdditions: Follow exports and imports across src/ until each candidate is proven to call or not call the retry helper.
Independently check the Conductor’s candidate list and state agreement or a concrete evidence-backed disagreement.
members.reasonForInclusion: Without this member, wrappers and re-export chains could hide callers that a lexical search would miss.

blueprint.teamRationale: The split separates straightforward symbol usage from hidden wrapper and re-export paths while ensuring each conclusion receives an independent challenge.
blueprint.collaborationStrategy: The direct-call researcher and indirect-path researcher publish separate evidence lists, then each audits the other list; the Conductor resolves discrepancies and supplies the reconciled markdown and required JSON payload to Architect for FINDINGS.md.
openAssumptions: Architect will create FINDINGS.md from the reconciled report because the requested artifact is handled by Architect.
Line numbers should refer to the repository’s current source state.
